extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, representatives, and examiners handling requests for expedited examination at the Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for preparing, submitting, and determining requests for expedited patent/utility-model examination at the Korean Intellectual Property Office, including required documents, content of disclosures, timelines, complementation, and examiner procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of self-search results (number of prior arts)
rubrics_metrics.description: For expedited examination, more than four searched prior arts closest to the claimed invention shall be disclosed. However, where special conditions exist, such as no relevant prior arts are found in the new technical field, less than three search results may be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the searched prior art is directly related to the technical field or all components of the claimed invention, the description of the search result shall be recognized as appropriate. Additional search results from local IP centers may be submitted instead of self-search processes and results. Self-search results suffice if an examiner can easily comprehend them; strict adherence to Annexed Form no.5 wording is not required. Antipattern: omitting mandatory search-results content (see 'inappropriately disclosed' below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrastive explanation content and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: In the contrastive explanation, the similarities, differences and contrastive analysis between each claim of the application for expedited examination and the closest prior art document to the concerned claim shall be described consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrastive explanations of all independent claims shall be described; contrastive explanation of dependent claims may be left out. If an independent claim's contrastive explanation is not disclosed but involves the same components as another disclosed independent claim (but in a different category), the undisclosed independent claim may be deemed appropriately described based on the disclosed one.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes inappropriate disclosure of self-search and contrastive explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-search results are inappropriately disclosed where any mandatory contents are not disclosed (① search processes and search results (more than four results), independent claims; ② contrastive explanation is inappropriately disclosed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If self-search results and contrastive explanation are not submitted or inappropriately disclosed, an examiner shall order supplementation. Failure to respond, failure to submit after response, or continued inappropriate disclosure can result in rejection of the request for expedited examination. Note: an examiner finding additional prior arts denying novelty/inventive step does not necessarily mean the self-search was inappropriately conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency standard for self-search results and contrastive explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-search results and contrastive explanation would suffice if an examiner can easily comprehend the results and explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants need not strictly follow the written explanation format of Annexed Form no.5 if the examiner can recognize the substance. Applicants may explain special cases (e.g., no relevant prior art found) and, if recognizable, the materials can be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing time calculation with excluded periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents to which an examiner cannot send a notification in response (e.g., report of change of applicant/representative, resignation reports) are received, the processing time shall be calculated excluding the period from receipt of the concerned documents to their acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: decision on expedited examination Feb 1; report of change submitted Mar 20; application accepted after amendment Apr 20 → expedited examination shall be conducted by May 3. In other words, expedited examination shall be conducted within two months from decision (for Article 4(1) or (2)), but adjust for periods where examination cannot be carried out (e.g., 32 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to attach to a written request for expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester shall attach the following to a written request for expedited examination in Annexed Form no.22: one original copy of a Written Explanation of Request for Expedited Examination (attached with evidential documents in annexed form) and one original copy of the evidential document of representation when proceeding is conducted by a representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit documents to the Customer Service Division of KIPO or the Application Registration Service Division of the Seoul Branch Office. Missing required attachments may lead to amendment orders or return/invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment requirements for request for expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester shall pay a fee for requesting expedited examination under the Collection Rules of Patent Fee, etc. to national treasury receipt banks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: electronically-filed applicants using the automated fee payment system need not pay fees in cash; fees are automatically transferred from a pre-registered financial institution account. To use automated payment, applicants must apply via the PatentRo website and file the application in electronic form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of third-party practicing conditions (Article 4(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person requesting expedited examination under Article 4(1) (third party's practicing of the invention per Article 61(1) of the Patent Act) shall specify the condition under which a third party practiced the claimed invention or utility model in a written explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidential documents that detail how/when a third party practiced the invention; complement orders will be issued if the evidence is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Annexed Form no.5 for Article 4(2) grounds and required items
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting expedited examination under Article 4(2) (applications under specified articles of Enforcement Decree), the requester shall fill out a Written Explanation in Annexed Form no.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items to indicate in Annexed Form no.5 include: (a) Self-search results and Contrastive explanation; (b) Ground for request of expedited examination; (c) Whether the claimed invention is being practiced (or prepared to be practiced) and whether practiced as business when requested under Article 4(2)(i); (d) Whether claimed invention is related to the type of business of a certified company (venture, INNO-BIZ, etc.); (e) Whether the claimed invention is funded or certified related to green technology (for Article 4(2)(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms for applications agreed between KIPO and foreign patent offices (Article 4(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications agreed for expedited examination between KIPO and a foreign patent office, the requester shall fill out Written Explanation in annexed forms no.2, no.3, or no.6 according to guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the relevant annexed form instructions per the applicable international/agreement guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of written explanation by authorized prior art search request (Article 4(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where expedited examination is requested on the ground that prior art search is requested to an authorized prior art search institute, an applicant can replace the written explanation by indicating that the prior art search has been requested to an authorized prior art search institute and stating the institute's name and date of request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate this in a request for expedited examination under Annexed Form no.22 of the Enforcement Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-availability of withdrawal after decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a notification of a decision of expedited examination has been made, a request for expedited examination shall not be withdrawn because once an examiner notifies a decision, the request takes effect and the examiner/KIPO starts examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a written withdrawal is submitted after the decision, the examiner shall notify the requester that withdrawal cannot be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination and response period for irregularities
rubrics_metrics.description: The person in charge shall conduct formalities examination on the request and transferred documents. When irregularities are found (statutory formalities not complied with or fees unpaid), the person in charge shall order amendment or notify a ground for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated period for submission of a written argument (amendment) or written explanation is one month, and the argument/explanation shall specify irregularities in detail. If irregularities fall under Article 11 of Enforcement Rules, notify ground for rejection; otherwise, order amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination after supplementation and treatment of late submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: After the designated period, if irregularities are deemed addressed based on submitted argument/amendment/explanation, the person in charge shall determine whether the application is eligible for expedited examination; if not addressed, invalidate the proceeding or return documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if submissions are late (after the designated period), the person in charge may treat them as valid written opinion/amendment/explanation and reassess eligibility rather than immediately invalidating/returning the proceeding, provided the proceeding has not already been invalidated or returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee return on invalidation or return
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the proceeding of a request for expedited examination is invalidated or documents are returned, the whole amount of fee of request for expedited examination shall be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice on invalidation/return shall contain the intention to invalidate/return, information on administrative trial or lawsuit rights, amount of fees to be returned, and how to apply for fee return. If dismissal occurs after determination, returned fee shall be the request fee with the fee for determination extracted.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC assignment priority and examiner change
rubrics_metrics.description: When assignment of IPC is delayed it postpones designation of a person in charge of determination; assign IPC on an application requested for expedited examination with priority to regular patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent examiner intends to change the examiner responsible, they may file a request for change of responsible examiner provided eligibility for expedited examination is determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination deadline for expedited examination (7-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person in charge shall determine whether to conduct expedited examination within seven days from the transfer date of a written request for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases of amendment orders, correction orders, or consultation, recalculate seven days from the date of termination of the period designated or from the date documents were transferred to the person in charge, whichever is later. The period spent calculating the deadline shall not be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with relevant agencies when eligibility unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is hard to determine whether the application is eligible for expedited examination under Article 4, the person in charge shall request consultation from relevant agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use external consultation to resolve ambiguous eligibility grounds rather than unilaterally dismissing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementation order scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is deemed not eligible or submitted documents cannot clarify eligibility, a person in charge shall order complementation of the request within one month. Items available for complementation are not limited and complementation may occur until determination; however, changing the application or the requester is not recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If complementation concerns prior art search failure, notify both requester and the specialized institute. Do not order complementation merely because the explanation doesn't comply with the annexed form. If irregularities remain after complementation, dismiss the request and notify requester and applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of determination outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application is eligible for expedited examination under Article 4, the person in charge shall notify the requester and applicant immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: patent applications agreed for expedited examination with foreign patent offices are not notified. For non-electronic relevant documents, the examiner must notify requester of final results and transmit documents to the principal director for electronic conversion. If documents are electronic, conversion/transmission step can be skipped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests made on multiple grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for expedited examination can be made on multiple grounds; if the requester holds at least one ground for request, the examiner shall not invalidate the request and shall determine and proceed with expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a ground claimed is insufficient but another ground exists among those submitted, proceed based on any valid ground. If a ground not claimed is obvious or explained enough, it may be considered, but determination is generally based on grounds indicated in the explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple requests and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a new request for expedited examination is submitted before the examiner determines on a previously-submitted request, the subsequently-submitted request shall be returned (treated like dual requests). After return/invalidation, a request may be submitted again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent duplicate requests before determination are returned to avoid multiple concurrent proceedings for same application. If requirements are fulfilled through complementation before the complementation deadline, determination can be made early; however dismissal determinations wait until the deadline expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing period after determination (start-of-examination deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall start examination on an application determined for expedited examination either within two months from the transmittal date of a written decision on expedited examination (four months for certain agreed/authorized-search cases) or within one month from the transmittal date of the search results to the examiner, whichever expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In principle, examine applications whose processing period expires first, but order may be changed for effective proceeding. If amendments are submitted before examination, the start may be within one month from transmittal of amendment. For super-expedited examination, start within fourteen days. If processing deadline cannot be met due to a jump in requests, report to the director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of final processing results and document handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The person in charge shall notify a requester (when not the applicant) of the final processing results on the application determined for expedited examination (grant, register, reject, withdrawal, abandonment, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant expedited-exam documents are not in electronic form, the examiner must notify and transmit documents for electronic conversion to the principal director. Electronic documents may skip this step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-case timing rules (deferral, divisional applications, pre-start requests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various special timing rules apply: (i) For applications filed before June 30, 2001 and requested by third party, defer determination for three months after filing. (ii) For divisional applications of a parent requested for expedited examination, the start time for the divisional (if not itself requested) is calculated based on the date of request for examination on the original application. (iii) If expedited request is made after examination has started and the application is eligible, treat as if requested and conduct expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For divisional applications requested for expedited examination, start according to earlier examination order between divisional and original. For prior-filed applications claiming domestic priority, in many cases requests may be invalidated unless priority is withdrawn per guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications being practiced by a third party — subject inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications deemed to have been practiced as business by a third party after laying-open of the application shall be included as subjects eligible under the 'practiced by third party' ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application has not been laid-open, the applicant should request early publication. Definitions: 'laying-open' per Article 64; 'third party' = person other than applicant who has not obtained permission to practice the claimed invention; 'practicing' refers to acts under Article 2(3) (manufacturing, using, assigning, leasing, importing, offering for assignment/lease, etc.).
